title: Depression
diagnosis: Major Depressive Disorder is the most likely diagnosis for a patient presenting with Depression of unknown etiology.
correct_orders: Laboratory workup (CBC, Chemistry Panel, TSH, Urinalysis)
should_avoid: Prescribing medications without proper evaluation and consultation

rationale.Psychiatric Consult: To assess the severity of depression, rule out other psychiatric disorders, and guide further management.
rationale.Laboratory workup: To evaluate for potential physical causes of depression or complications (e.g., electrolyte imbalance, thyroid dysfunction), and to monitor treatment response.
rationale.Psychological Evaluation: To assess the patient's psychological state and functioning, which can aid in diagnosis and treatment planning.

physical_exam: Depression — exam tailored to chief complaint on arrival.
Soft, non-distended, no focal peritoneal signs on initial exam.
Alert and oriented unless perfusion or metabolic derangement present.
No acute rash; capillary refill and perfusion assessed.
order_sets: Laboratory workup (CBC, Chemistry Panel, TSH, Urinalysis)
